content:
A few weeks ago I started learning more about "Cobham's axioms", a relatively simple characterization of the class of polynomial time functions. I thought this seemed like a nice concept, and I found it useful for another formalization project I was working on. Would this be a good addition to CSLib?

I think the only time I ever saw something like this before was in this thread #general > cook levin, np completeness of SAT @ 💬 from @Palalansoukî (sorry for ignoring it at the time). @Palalansoukî have you or anyone else made progress on implementing function algebras anywhere?
I would love to see this in CSLib

I had been working on this personally in my private repository (the name "unrelativizable" comes from my attempt to formalize the classic result that P vs. NP is unrelativizable, due to Baker, Gill and Solovay), but at this very early stage, it’s essentially just a set of definitions. I’ve been busy with FFL for a while and haven’t been able to work on it.

If anyone else is interested in taking this on, I think that would be great. To me, this seems like the only realistic way to tackle poly-time functions. At the very least, it’s far better than dealing with TM directly.
I think we should do both this type of thing and TMs directly.
With a bridge connecting them via proofs that TMs satisfy the axioms.
CSLib#899 is a draft PR, (there are still some design decisions I have to think through).
